newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Pakistani troops still firing in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: India says Pakistani troops still firing in Kashmir.

text.p: Heavy firing and shelling by Pakistani troops from across the border continued for the fifth consecutive day in India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state on Sunday, an Indian defence spokesman said.
Brigadier Sunil Kapoor of the Indian army said: "The firing and shelling by Pakistani troops across the border continued till 12:30 p.m (0700 GMT) on Sunday in Kargil sector."

There were no casualties on Sunday, he said. Pakistani troops had been firing on the Kargil region of mountainous Ladakh since Wednesday, he added. Kargil is 220 km (150 miles) southwest of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
The intermittent shooting in Kargil has forced at least 4,000 people to abandon their homes. Two residents of Kargil, including a child, were killed on Friday and eight civilians seriously injured.
Pakistani defence officials said nothing unusual had happened and that exchanges of fire between Indian and Pakistani troops were routine.
The two countries have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain 50 years ago over disputed Kashmir.
The "working" border between India and Pakistan stretches 174 km (109 miles) between the Chenab and Ravi rivers to join up in the north with the Line of Control, or ceasefire line, dividing Kashmir.
